stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."

    # Reuses the fresh coverage/lcov.info produced by the coverage stage.
    # Hook mode scopes the analysis to the STAGED lib/bin files: the
    # ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a pre-existing offender in

    # whole-repo analyze, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.
    local files=""

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."

    # Hook mode scopes the analysis to the STAGED lib/bin files: the
    # ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a pre-existing offender in

    local files=""

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

ensure_app_placeholders() {

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders
    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_crap() {
  if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     dart pub global run crap4dart --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking CRAP scores (ratchet pinned in crap4dart.yaml)..."
    # Reuses the fresh coverage/lcov.info produced by the coverage stage.
    # Hook mode scopes the analysis to the STAGED lib/bin files: the
    # ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a pre-existing offender in
    # an untouched file cannot block an unrelated commit. CI keeps the
    # whole-repo analyze, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.
    local files=""
    if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
      files=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
        | grep -E '^(lib|bin)/.*\.dart$' || true)
      if [ -z "$files" ]; then
        echo "   no staged lib/bin sources — nothing to ratchet"
        return 0
      fi
      echo "   hook scope: $(echo "$files" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') staged file(s)"
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart analyze $files; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — CRAP RATCHET" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      return 0
    fi
    if ! dart pub global run crap4dart analyze; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — CRAP RATCHET" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  else
    return 2  # caller prints SKIP marker
  fi
}

stage_dup() {
  if ! command -v jscpd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 2  # caller prints SKIP marker
  fi
  echo "🔍 Checking code duplication (core < ${DUP_THRESHOLD}%, flutter_app < ${DUP_THRESHOLD_APP}%)..."
  local core_dup app_dup dup_ok=1
  dup_pct() {
    jscpd --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json --output "$2" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    python3 -c "
import json
try:
    with open('$2/jscpd-report.json') as f:
        d=json.load(f)
    print(d['statistics']['total']['percentage'])
except Exception:
    print('0.0')
" 2>/dev/null || echo "0.0"
  }
  core_dup=$(dup_pct lib/ /tmp/jscpd-fastgate-core)
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    app_dup=$(dup_pct flutter_app/lib/ /tmp/jscpd-fastgate-app)
  else
    app_dup="0.0"
  fi
  if python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$core_dup') < float('$DUP_THRESHOLD') else 1)"; then
    echo "✅ Core duplication check OK ($core_dup% < ${DUP_THRESHOLD}%)"
  else
    dup_ok=0
  fi
  if python3 -c "exit(0 if float('$app_dup') < float('$DUP_THRESHOLD_APP') else 1)"; then
    echo "✅ flutter_app duplication check OK ($app_dup% < ${DUP_THRESHOLD_APP}%)"
  else
    dup_ok=0
  fi
  if [ "$dup_ok" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — CODE DUPLICATION (core $core_dup%, flutter_app $app_dup%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

1. **`_textFromStdout` on Windows PowerShell output encoding**: `Get-Clipboard` output through PowerShell stdout captured as raw bytes then utf8-decoded — PowerShell 5.1 on Windows outputs UTF-16LE by default for the console... Actually `[Console]::OutputEncoding` — when captured via a pipe, PowerShell uses the OEM code page or UTF-8 depending on config. `Process.start` without runInShell captures raw bytes; PowerShell 5.1 writes the default output encoding (usually the console code page, OEM 437 in US) — non-ASCII text may mojibake. The image reader on Windows already uses PowerShell the same way. This is a pre-existing platform limitation; for text it can garble non-ASCII (e.g. "café" → mojibake). For `-Command` output redirected to a pipe, PowerShell 5.1 uses `[Console]::OutputEncoding` which defaults to the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850) — NOT UTF-8. So non-ASCII clipboard text would mojibake on Windows. A robust fix: `-Command '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard'` — but pwsh 7 defaults to UTF-8. This is a real (if platform-untestable) correctness nit → SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The PR description says "Windows newline strip" tested. Given CI can't test Windows clipboard, and Windows TUI use is niche... I'd file as SUGGESTION. Hmm, but "Ctrl+V with accented text on Windows mojibakes" is a real user-facing bug. It's the kind of thing reviewers should flag. I'll mark IMPORTANT? Let me think about severity: it silently corrupts pasted text on a whole platform. Hmm wait, actually let me double check: `Get-Clipboard` in PowerShell 5.1 outputs text; when piped, PowerShell uses its own formatting → emits lines with the console output encoding. Yes — for redirected output PS 5.1 uses OEM codepage by default. So é (U+00E9) becomes 0x82 in cp437 → utf8.decode(allowMalformed) → U+FFFD replacement char. Real mojibake. IMPORTANT.

But wait — one real behavior difference: `xclip -o` outputs the text WITH a trailing newline typically? xclip outputs exactly the clipboard content; if the user copied text without trailing newline, xclip adds one? Actually xclip -o prints selection content as-is (with an added newline in some versions?). Historically xclip adds a trailing newline unless... there's no --no-newline for xclip (wl-paste has --no-newline). macOS pbpaste preserves exactly. So on Linux, pasted text may gain a trailing \n. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2

  fi
}

stage_crap() {
  if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     dart pub global run crap4dart --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking CRAP scores (ratchet pinned in crap4dart.yaml)..."
    # Reuses the fresh coverage/lcov.info produced by the coverage stage.
    # Hook mode scopes the analysis to the STAGED lib/bin files: the
    # ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a pre-existing offender in
    # an untouched file cannot block an unrelated commit. CI keeps the
    # whole-repo analyze, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.
    local files=""
    if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then

    app_dup=$(dup_pct flutter_app/lib/ /tmp/jscpd-fastgate-app)

    echo "✅ flutter_app duplication check OK ($app_dup% < ${DUP_THRESHOLD_APP}%)"

    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — CODE DUPLICATION (core $core_dup%, flutter_app $app_dup%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"

  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

Now I understand the gate structure. The "CRAP + duplication" CI job = stage_crap + stage_dup. The failure could be:
1. CRAP ratchet: a new method with CRAP score > 12.0 given coverage. `readPasteboardText`, `_textFromStdout`, `_readLinuxText`, `_readWindowsText`, `_convertTiffToPng`, `_osascriptClipboardClassToFile` — all in clipboard_reader.dart. CRAP = comp + (comp-1)(1-cov)^... formula: CRAP = CC^2 * (1-coverage)^3 + CC for changed. Which of these functions are covered by the new tests?

The tests cover: TIFF success, TIFF conversion failure, text macos path (pbpaste hit + empty), linux fallback (xclip fail → wl-paste hit), windows strip, linux both fail. What's NOT covered:
- `_readWindowsText` — the "text is PasteboardText but doesn't end with newline" branch (text not ending with \r\n or \n)? Test only covers '\r\n' ending. The `else if text.endsWith('\n')` branch is NOT covered. Also `if (text.isEmpty) return unavailable` after strip — not covered.
- `_textFromStdout` exitCode != 0 branch — covered? In the linux fallback test, calls==1 returns ProcessResult(1, 1, '', 'nope') — that hits exitCode != 0. Covered.
- `_textFromStdout` `stdout is List<int>` false branch — the fake runner `_ok(utf8.encode(...))` returns bytes. `utf8.encode('$stdout')` branch not covered.
- `readPasteboardText` catch on Object — not covered (ProcessException path).
- `readPasteboardText` final `return const PasteboardUnavailable('no pasteboard reader for this platform')` — only reached when platform is unknown. Test exists for image path but for text? "the pinned platform falls through to the platform note" is for image. So for text: `_effectivePlatform` returning null branch is not covered in text tests. 

Hmm — CRAP score with 0% coverage: CRAP = CC^2 + CC. For CC=3 → 12. `_readWindowsText`: CC? branches: read is! PasteboardText (1), endsWith \r\n (2), endsWith \n (3), isEmpty (4) → CC=4 → if 0% covered: 16+4=20 > 12! But wait — the windows test DOES call _readWindowsText (the strip test). Coverage of _readWindowsText: the test covers the '\r\n' branch → some coverage. CRAP formula uses covered ratio: crap = crap1(coverage, cc) = cc^2 * (1 - coverage)^3 + cc where coverage is fraction covered. If the test covers most paths but not all branches... coverage here is LINE coverage from lcov with branch_coverage: true. Hmm.

Actually wait — is `coverage/lcov.info` required: true. The CI regenerates coverage before CRAP. The CI run for the failed check — I can't see the log. Let me try running the CRAP analysis locally. Need to install crap4dart (pinned >=0.11.0 <0.12.0) and run the tests to generate coverage. The full test suite is 10547 tests — heavy. But maybe I can run just the relevant test files with coverage and format lcov, then run crap4dart analyze on the file.

Actually, simpler approach: run crap4dart with coverage from just the clipboard tests to compute the CRAP scores of the changed functions. But the whole-repo lcov determines coverage of each method. For clipboard_reader.dart methods, coverage comes from clipboard_reader_test.dart and other tests that hit those functions (fa_tui_paste_flow_test, PTY goldens...).

Alternatively, let me look at the failed CI runs via the URL. No network access to GitHub API? There's dmtools maybe. Let me try to fetch the CI job log via dmtools or gh CLI. Actually, let me check if gh is available and authenticated.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.
