## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

blocks.text:
The conditional import in `agent_cli.dart:237` makes `readPasteboardText` resolve to the stub on web — the web-safe wiring is correct.

Now, one more correctness angle: **`_handlePasteboardResult`'s new `PasteboardText` branch ignores `prompt != null`** — could a PasteboardResultMsg land while a prompt is open? The probe is only fired from `_handlePasteImageKey` (normal mode; prompt routes earlier) and `_handlePaste` (which in prompt mode returns early before firing). But an in-flight probe from BEFORE entering prompt mode could deliver its message while a prompt is open → `editor.insert` behind the prompt → text silently lands in the composer, not the prompt buffer. Edge case: user hits Ctrl+V then immediately `/` opens... actually slash menu isn't a prompt; prompts are dial/secret prompts. Ctrl+V → probe fires (async subprocess) → user opens a prompt within the ~50-200ms subprocess window → text lands in editor instead of prompt. Ultra-narrow race; the same race already exists for PasteboardImage chips (attachment chip while prompt open). Pre-existing class of race, not introduced here. Skip.

**Duplicate-probe semantics with the wrapped reader**: `_firePasteboardProbe` stamps the gesture; the wrapper closure runs inside the Cmd (off UI loop) — both image and text reads happen inside one Cmd. Gesture window unchanged. Good.

**`text.text.isNotEmpty` double-check in the wrapper**: `readPasteboardText` never returns empty PasteboardText, but the callback is injectable — the wrapper's guard is a legit defense; test "text fallback without a wired text reader" covers null. The `isNotEmpty` guard isn't directly tested (a textReader returning empty PasteboardText) — minor; skip.

Now **CRAP check on `fa_tui_paste.dart` `_handlePasteImageKey`**: added branches — CC up slightly; CI CRAP ratchet passed, so fine.

**Line-count fix guidance**: The repo precedent (see fa_tui_paste.dart header): "split out of fa_tui.dart to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate". The 7 added lines must come out of fa_tui.dart — options: shorten the readClipboardText doc comment (7 lines of doc → 2), or move an existing zone out. That's for the author; my review flags the failure + the evidence + fix options.

Wait — actually let me double check what exactly was added to fa_tui.dart: +1 ctor line, +6 doc/field lines = 7 lines. Trimming the doc comment to ~2 lines gets to 2803 — still over! 2807 - 2800 = 7 over. Even zeroing the doc comment leaves the field + ctor param = 2 lines over. So a doc-trim alone is insufficient; the author must move something out (another zone split) or the field must live elsewhere. Hmm, interesting: they can't avoid adding the field to fa_tui.dart's FaTuiCallbacks (the real one). So the fix REQUIRES moving ~9+ existing lines out of fa_tui.dart (e.g. move `PasteboardResultMsg` class — it's defined in fa_tui_paste.dart already... it's `part of fa_tui.dart` so moving between parts doesn't change the file's line count for the loc gate? The loc gate counts LINES PER FILE — `fa_tui_paste.dart` is a separate file (part file). Moving `PasteboardResultMsg` (≈11 lines) from fa_tui.dart... wait it's already in fa_tui_paste.dart. Let me check what's IN fa_tui.dart that could move: maybe some zone or the FaTuiCallbacks class itself could move to a new part file. Whatever — the author decides; I'll note the constraint (7 over; a doc-comment trim alone won't fit, needs ≥9 lines relocated — e.g. move a small helper/class into an existing part file like fa_tui_paste.dart).

Let me verify where PasteboardResultMsg lives and confirm fa_tui_paste.dart is a part:  yes — `part of 'fa_tui.dart';` (line 4 of fa_tui_paste.dart). So moving `PasteboardResultMsg` (currently in fa_tui_paste.dart) would ADD lines to... no wait, it's already in the part file. I mean moving something from fa_tui.dart INTO a part file. E.g. move `FaTuiCallbacks` (huge) — no. Simplest: move the `_pasteboardGestureWindowMs` const? Already in paste part. OK the author will figure it out; options: relocate a self-contained helper/extension into an existing part file (part files don't count against fa_tui.dart's 2807).

Alright. Now **exhaustive pass** on the changed files for anything else:

1. `CHANGELOG.md` — entry added under Unreleased; accurate; matches style of neighboring entries (multi-line wrapped). Good.

2. `clipboard_reader.dart` doc comment at top: "macOS: osascript writes «class PNGf» (fallback «class JPEG»)... a third «class TIFF» probe" — accurate. The FA_FAKE_PASTEBOARD bullet now slightly overclaims ("short-circuits everything") since readPasteboardText ignores it — SUGGESTION (doc drift).

3. `_readMacos` — TIFF probe placed AFTER the PNGf/JPEG loop, so a pasteboard holding BOTH PNGf and TIFF prefers PNGf. Correct priority (PNGf lossless vs TIFF conversion lossy-ish). Good design.

4. `_osascriptClipboardClassToFile` — on success deletes scratch file; on osascript success but file-read failure (catch) → returns null, file may remain (delete failed inside try? `File(target).readAsBytesSync(); File(target).deleteSync();` — if read throws, delete never runs → orphan file; if delete throws, file remains). Best-effort as before (pre-existing behavior). Not worth a finding — well, actually the old code was identical in shape. Skip.

5. `_convertTiffToPng` — `finally` cleanup loop: `file.existsSync()` then deleteSync — TOCTOU irrelevant here. Fine. Note: if sips succeeded but readAsBytesSync throws (racing delete?), covered by catch → null. Fine.

6. sips PNG validation: sips conversion output is trusted as PNG without magic-byte re-check downstream? `pasteImageError` sniffs magic bytes — `sniffImageMime` checks PNG magic — a corrupt conversion → sniff fails → named error 'clipboard does not hold a recognized image'. Defense exists downstream in _handlePasteboardResult (pasteImageError). Good.

7. `readPasteboardText` — doc says "Empty stdout counts as no text" — implemented in _textFromStdout. Windows strip-then-empty also handled. Good.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1580
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1580

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1580
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1580
- **Title**: gh-1575 [BUG] macOS clipboard image: TIFF-only pasteboard reports no image Ctrl+V ignores text clipboard
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1580
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1580

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1580

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

blocks.text:
The conditional import in `agent_cli.dart:237` makes `readPasteboardText` resolve to the stub on web — the web-safe wiring is correct.

Now, one more correctness angle: **`_handlePasteboardResult`'s new `PasteboardText` branch ignores `prompt != null`** — could a PasteboardResultMsg land while a prompt is open? The probe is only fired from `_handlePasteImageKey` (normal mode; prompt routes earlier) and `_handlePaste` (which in prompt mode returns early before firing). But an in-flight probe from BEFORE entering prompt mode could deliver its message while a prompt is open → `editor.insert` behind the prompt → text silently lands in the composer, not the prompt buffer. Edge case: user hits Ctrl+V then immediately `/` opens... actually slash menu isn't a prompt; prompts are dial/secret prompts. Ctrl+V → probe fires (async subprocess) → user opens a prompt within the ~50-200ms subprocess window → text lands in editor instead of prompt. Ultra-narrow race; the same race already exists for PasteboardImage chips (attachment chip while prompt open). Pre-existing class of race, not introduced here. Skip.

**Duplicate-probe semantics with the wrapped reader**: `_firePasteboardProbe` stamps the gesture; the wrapper closure runs inside the Cmd (off UI loop) — both image and text reads happen inside one Cmd. Gesture window unchanged. Good.

**`text.text.isNotEmpty` double-check in the wrapper**: `readPasteboardText` never returns empty PasteboardText, but the callback is injectable — the wrapper's guard is a legit defense; test "text fallback without a wired text reader" covers null. The `isNotEmpty` guard isn't directly tested (a textReader returning empty PasteboardText) — minor; skip.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

Actually, Console.OpenStandardOutput + TextWriter with the encoding — .NET's Console class does not write the BOM to stdout. Empirically, `powershell -Command "[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; 'hi'"` does not emit a BOM at the start of piped output. Hmm, is that certain? There ARE known reports that PowerShell 5.1 with UTF8 OutputEncoding emits BOM when redirecting... The BOM reports are about `Out-File`/redirect to file (`>`), which defaults to UTF-16LE or writes BOMs. For console output encoding, the .NET Console encoder strips the preamble (Console.cs uses a StreamWriter with `encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: false`? — Actually Console's OutputEncoding creates the writer with `TextWriter.OutputEncoding`... I recall the console output writer is constructed with the encoding and does write the preamble when the encoding provides one... Let me think again: `Console.OutputEncoding` setter recreates the stdout writer via `__ConsoleStream` + `StreamWriter(..., encoding)`. The StreamWriter constructor default `detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks` writes the preamble lazily... StreamWriter writes the preamble on first write IF the encoding has one (GetPreamble().Length > 0), unless constructed with a specific flag. Hmm — StreamWriter(Stream, Encoding) DOES emit the preamble. But there's a special case: Console.Out is created via `CreateOutputWriter` which uses `new StreamWriter(stream, new ConsoleEncoding(encoding), ...)` — .NET has an internal `ConsoleEncoding` wrapper class whose `GetPreamble()` returns **empty** precisely to avoid BOMs on console streams! Yes — that's a real .NET internal (ConsoleEncoding : Encoding, wraps and returns Array.Empty<byte>() for GetPreamble). So no BOM on console output. Good — no BOM concern.

   Even if a BOM did sneak in: utf8.decode would render it as U+FEFF at the start of the composer text — minor cosmetic. Not confident enough to file; skip.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1575: macOS clipboard paste fixed for TIFF-only pasteboards + the
  Ctrl+V text fallback. `_readMacos` probes `«class TIFF»` after PNGf/JPEG
  miss and converts via `sips -s format png` (a Preview/browser copy used
  to dead-end on `clipboard holds no image`; a failed conversion keeps the
  unavailable fall-through and every scratch file is cleaned up); new
  `readPasteboardText` (`pbpaste` / xclip+wl-paste / PowerShell
  Get-Clipboard) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:`
  seam, and Ctrl+V with a TEXT clipboard now inserts the clipboard text
  into the composer instead of printing the image probe's dead-end reason
  — bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing and silent-failure semantics
  unchanged. Review pass: the Windows `Get-Clipboard` read pins UTF-8
  console output and normalizes embedded `\r\n` (OEM-code-page mojibake),
  the Linux text backends pin `text/plain;charset=utf-8` (an image-only
  clipboard can no longer leak bytes as "text"), the library doc no longer
  overclaims the `FA_FAKE_PASTEBOARD` seam, and `FaTuiCallbacks` moved to
  a `fa_tui_callbacks.dart` part file keeping `fa_tui.dart` under the
  2800-line gate.

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter

The conditional import in `agent_cli.dart:237` makes `readPasteboardText` resolve to the stub on web — the web-safe wiring is correct.

Now, one more correctness angle: **`_handlePasteboardResult`'s new `PasteboardText` branch ignores `prompt != null`** — could a PasteboardResultMsg land while a prompt is open? The probe is only fired from `_handlePasteImageKey` (normal mode; prompt routes earlier) and `_handlePaste` (which in prompt mode returns early before firing). But an in-flight probe from BEFORE entering prompt mode could deliver its message while a prompt is open → `editor.insert` behind the prompt → text silently lands in the composer, not the prompt buffer. Edge case: user hits Ctrl+V then immediately `/` opens... actually slash menu isn't a prompt; prompts are dial/secret prompts. Ctrl+V → probe fires (async subprocess) → user opens a prompt within the ~50-200ms subprocess window → text lands in editor instead of prompt. Ultra-narrow race; the same race already exists for PasteboardImage chips (attachment chip while prompt open). Pre-existing class of race, not introduced here. Skip.

**Duplicate-probe semantics with the wrapped reader**: `_firePasteboardProbe` stamps the gesture; the wrapper closure runs inside the Cmd (off UI loop) — both image and text reads happen inside one Cmd. Gesture window unchanged. Good.

**`text.text.isNotEmpty` double-check in the wrapper**: `readPasteboardText` never returns empty PasteboardText, but the callback is injectable — the wrapper's guard is a legit defense; test "text fallback without a wired text reader" covers null. The `isNotEmpty` guard isn't directly tested (a textReader returning empty PasteboardText) — minor; skip.

Now **CRAP check on `fa_tui_paste.dart` `_handlePasteImageKey`**: added branches — CC up slightly; CI CRAP ratchet passed, so fine.

**Line-count fix guidance**: The repo precedent (see fa_tui_paste.dart header): "split out of fa_tui.dart to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate". The 7 added lines must come out of fa_tui.dart — options: shorten the readClipboardText doc comment (7 lines of doc → 2), or move an existing zone out. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1575: macOS clipboard paste fixed for TIFF-only pasteboards + the
  Ctrl+V text fallback. `_readMacos` probes `«class TIFF»` after PNGf/JPEG
  miss and converts via `sips -s format png` (a Preview/browser copy used

  Get-Clipboard) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:`

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1580
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1580
- **Title**: gh-1575 [BUG] macOS clipboard image: TIFF-only pasteboard reports no image Ctrl+V ignores text clipboard
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1575: macOS clipboard paste fixed for TIFF-only pasteboards + the
  Ctrl+V text fallback. `_readMacos` probes `«class TIFF»` after PNGf/JPEG
  miss and converts via `sips -s format png` (a Preview/browser copy used
  to dead-end on `clipboard holds no image`; a failed conversion keeps the
  unavailable fall-through and every scratch file is cleaned up); new
  `readPasteboardText` (`pbpaste` / xclip+wl-paste / PowerShell
  Get-Clipboard) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:`
  seam, and Ctrl+V with a TEXT clipboard now inserts the clipboard text
  into the composer instead of printing the image probe's dead-end reason
  — bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing and silent-failure semantics
  unchanged. Review pass: the Windows `Get-Clipboard` read pins UTF-8
  console output and normalizes embedded `\r\n` (OEM-code-page mojibake),
  the Linux text backends pin `text/plain;charset=utf-8` (an image-only
  clipboard can no longer leak bytes as "text"), the library doc no longer
  overclaims the `FA_FAKE_PASTEBOARD` seam, and `FaTuiCallbacks` moved to
  a `fa_tui_callbacks.dart` part file keeping `fa_tui.dart` under the
  2800-line gate.

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

When PowerShell writes text to a redirected stdout using Console.OutputEncoding, the .NET console encoder for UTF8 — `System.Text.Encoding.UTF8` has `GetPreamble()` = EF BB BF. Console output via OutputEncoding: the StreamWriter wrapping stdout — Console.Out uses AutoFlush and typically does NOT emit the preamble for stdout (the preamble is only written when using the encoding's GetPreamble explicitly, e.g., StreamWriter with a file). Actually, Console.OpenStandardOutput + TextWriter with the encoding — .NET's Console class does not write the BOM to stdout. # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1575: macOS clipboard paste fixed for TIFF-only pasteboards + the
  Ctrl+V text fallback. `_readMacos` probes `«class TIFF»` after PNGf/JPEG
  miss and converts via `sips -s format png` (a Preview/browser copy used
  to dead-end on `clipboard holds no image`; a failed conversion keeps the
  unavailable fall-through and every scratch file is cleaned up); new
  `readPasteboardText` (`pbpaste` / xclip+wl-paste / PowerShell
  Get-Clipboard) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:`
  seam, and Ctrl+V with a TEXT clipboard now inserts the clipboard text
  into the composer instead of printing the image probe's dead-end reason
  — bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing and silent-failure semantics
  unchanged. Review pass: the Windows `Get-Clipboard` read pins UTF-8
  console output and normalizes embedded `\r\n` (OEM-code-page mojibake),
  the Linux text backends pin `text/plain;charset=utf-8` (an image-only
  clipboard can no longer leak bytes as "text"), the library doc no longer
  overclaims the `FA_FAKE_PASTEBOARD` seam, and `FaTuiCallbacks` moved to
  a `fa_tui_callbacks.dart` part file keeping `fa_tui.dart` under the
  2800-line gate.

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1575` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +658
- **Deletions**: -146
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T09:57:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:48:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- gh-1575: macOS clipboard paste fixed for TIFF-only pasteboards + the
  Ctrl+V text fallback. `_readMacos` probes `«class TIFF»` after PNGf/JPEG
  miss and converts via `sips -s format png` (a Preview/browser copy used
  to dead-end on `clipboard holds no image`; a failed conversion keeps the
  unavailable fall-through and every scratch file is cleaned up); new
  `readPasteboardText` (`pbpaste` / xclip+wl-paste / PowerShell
  Get-Clipboard) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:`
  seam, and Ctrl+V with a TEXT clipboard now inserts the clipboard text
  into the composer instead of printing the image probe's dead-end reason
  — bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing and silent-failure semantics
  unchanged. Review pass: the Windows `Get-Clipboard` read pins UTF-8
  console output and normalizes embedded `\r\n` (OEM-code-page mojibake),
  the Linux text backends pin `text/plain;charset=utf-8` (an image-only
  clipboard can no longer leak bytes as "text"), the library doc no longer
  overclaims the `FA_FAKE_PASTEBOARD` seam, and `FaTuiCallbacks` moved to
  a `fa_tui_callbacks.dart` part file keeping `fa_tui.dart` under the
  2800-line gate.

- gh-1556: bench pipeline stops bleeding score + fa deadline awareness.
  Bench: the harbor ladder kill uses the `[f]a` bracket trick and is
  wrapped so a kill failure can never replace the `TimeoutError` (the
  pre-fix self-matching `pkill` classified TB 2.0 ladder kills as agent
  crashes — a SOLVED task scored 0); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per
  the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s) is the
  bench-harbor.yml default on every shard, with the harbor adapter

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Linux text backends are not type-pinned — an image-only clipboard can be dumped into the composer as garbage "text"**

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Windows text read is not UTF-8 — non-ASCII clipboard text mojibakes**

`Get-Clipboard` runs under `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1), whose redirected stdout is written in the OEM code page (e.g. cp437/cp850), **not** UTF-8. The output is then decoded as UTF-8 here with `allowMalformed: true`, so any non-ASCII clipboard text ("café", "Привет", CJK) silently degrades to U+FFFD replacement characters — exactly the lossy path this repo's image readers deliberately avoid: the pre-existing `_readWindows` image path never reads stdout (it writes a file and reads the bytes back, see `_readWindows` below in this file).

Secondary: `Get-Clipboard` formats each line with `\r\n`, so multi-line text keeps embedded `\r` after the single trailing-newline strip; the composer inserts verbatim (no `\r` normalization exists in the TUI paste path).

**Suggested fix** (mirror the image path's stdout avoidance, or pin the encoding):

```dart
final read = _textFromStdout(
  await runner('powershell', [
    '-NoProfile',
    '-Command',
    '[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard',
  ]),
);
```

and normalize embedded `\r\n` → `\n` alongside the trailing strip. Untestable on the Linux CI runner, so at minimum worth a follow-up card — but as written, the Windows Ctrl+V text fallback corrupts everything outside ASCII.

The image path pins explicit content types (`xclip … -t image/png`, `wl-paste --type image/png`), but the new text loop does not:

- `xclip -selection clipboard -o` defaults to `STRING`; on a clipboard that holds only image flavors it errors out (fine).
- `wl-paste --no-newline` **without `--type` pastes the first MIME type offered by the source** — for an image-only clipboard that is `image/png`/`image/jpeg`, exit code 0, stdout = raw image bytes.

Trigger path: clipboard holds only a non-PNG image (e.g. JPEG-only — the image reader only probes `image/png`), so `readPasteboardImage` misses → the Ctrl+V fallback runs → `wl-paste --no-newline` happily returns the image bytes → `_textFromStdout` decodes them with `allowMalformed: true` → a wall of mojibake `PasteboardText` is inserted into the composer (and one keypress away from being submitted).

**Suggested fix** — pin text types the way the image path does:

```dart
for (final (executable, args) in [
  ('xclip', ['-selection', 'clipboard', '-t', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '-o']),
  ('wl-paste', ['--type', 'text/plain;charset=utf-8', '--no-newline']),
]) {
```

With explicit types, an image-only clipboard fails both backends and keeps the correct named `'xclip/wl-paste unavailable or clipboard holds no text'` reason instead of pasting binary garbage.

## PR Description

Closes #1575
### Root Cause

`_readMacos` in `lib/src/cli/clipboard_reader.dart` probed only `«class PNGf»`/`«class JPEG»` — a TIFF-only pasteboard (Preview/browser copies) fails both and reports `clipboard holds no image`. Ctrl+V also fired only the image probe and returned, so a TEXT clipboard had no paste path at all.

### Fix

- `clipboard_reader.dart`: after PNGf/JPEG miss, probe `«class TIFF»` and convert to PNG via `sips -s format png <in> --out <out>`; conversion output becomes `PasteboardImage`, conversion failure keeps the `PasteboardUnavailable` fall-through; scratch files cleaned up.
- `clipboard_reader.dart`: new `readPasteboardText()` (`pbpaste` / `xclip`+`wl-paste` / PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`) behind the same injectable `ProcessRunner`/`platform:` seam; empty stdout = named unavailable.
- `paste_image.dart`: pure `PasteboardText` variant of the sealed `PasteboardRead` family.
- `fa_tui_paste.dart`: Ctrl+V wraps the image probe — image hit → chip (unchanged); miss → text read → inserted into the composer; neither → original named reason. New `readClipboardText` callback (real + web stub), wired in `agent_cli_repl_boot.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `clipboard_reader_test.dart`: TIFF-only macOS → sips output used; failed conversion → unavailable; `readPasteboardText` per-platform (pbpaste hit/empty, xclip→wl-paste fallback, Windows newline strip).
- `fa_tui_paste_flow_test.dart`: text clipboard inserts; image preferred (text reader untouched); both miss → named reason; no text reader → legacy behavior.
- Full suite: 10547 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- Bracketed-paste routing, gesture pairing (#1067) and silent-failure semantics unchanged; the text fallback rides Ctrl+V only.

When PowerShell writes text to a redirected stdout using Console.OutputEncoding, the .NET console encoder for UTF8 — `System.Text.Encoding.UTF8` has `GetPreamble()` = EF BB BF. Console output via OutputEncoding: the StreamWriter wrapping stdout — Console.Out uses AutoFlush and typically does NOT emit the preamble for stdout (the preamble is only written when using the encoding's GetPreamble explicitly, e.g., StreamWriter with a file). Actually, Console.OpenStandardOutput + TextWriter with the encoding — .NET's Console class does not write the BOM to stdout. Empirically, `powershell -Command "[Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; 'hi'"` does not emit a BOM at the start of piped output. Hmm, is that certain? There ARE known reports that PowerShell 5.1 with UTF8 OutputEncoding emits BOM when redirecting... The BOM reports are about `Out-File`/redirect to file (`>`), which defaults to UTF-16LE or writes BOMs. For console output encoding, the .NET Console encoder strips the preamble (Console.cs uses a StreamWriter with `encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: false`? — Actually Console's OutputEncoding creates the writer with `TextWriter.OutputEncoding`... I recall the console output writer is constructed with the encoding and does write the preamble when the encoding provides one... Let me think again: `Console.OutputEncoding` setter recreates the stdout writer via `__ConsoleStream` + `StreamWriter(..., encoding)`. The StreamWriter constructor default `detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks` writes the preamble lazily... StreamWriter writes the preamble on first write IF the encoding has one (GetPreamble().Length > 0), unless constructed with a specific flag. Hmm — StreamWriter(Stream, Encoding) DOES emit the preamble. But there's a special case: Console.Out is created via `CreateOutputWriter` which uses `new StreamWriter(stream, new ConsoleEncoding(encoding), ...)` — .NET has an internal `ConsoleEncoding` wrapper class whose `GetPreamble()` returns **empty** precisely to avoid BOMs on console streams!
